Scope and source

Source page: eCFR, 12 CFR Part 217, Subpart B, § 217.10, https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-II/subchapter-A/part-217/section-217.10 (fetched 2026-11-23T11:52:58Z, sha256 11713cd13188). Corroborated by the eCFR Subpart B page and the govinfo 2026 CFR text of Part 217. The operative provision is 12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1).

Period: the regulatory minimums in the cited current text as of 2026-11-23. These are ongoing regulatory floors, not fiscal-period financial data. Currency: the ratios are dimensionless percentages; the underlying capital and exposure amounts are in USD as reported by the institution. Basis: risk-weighted assets for the CET1, Tier 1 and Total capital ratios; average total consolidated assets for the leverage ratio; total leverage exposure for the supplementary leverage ratio.

Answer before buffers or add-ons

| Ratio | Minimum | Source | Basis and arithmetic | Check |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Common equity tier 1 capital ratio | 4.5% | § 217.10(a)(1)(i) | CET1 capital divided by standardized total risk-weighted assets, § 217.10(b)(1). Arithmetic: 4.5% = 4.5 / 100 = 0.045. | Bare minimum; no buffer included. |
| Tier 1 capital ratio | 6% | § 217.10(a)(1)(ii) | Tier 1 capital divided by standardized total risk-weighted assets, § 217.10(b)(2). Arithmetic: 6% = 6 / 100 = 0.06. | Bare minimum; no buffer included. |
| Total capital ratio | 8% | § 217.10(a)(1)(iii) | Total capital divided by standardized total risk-weighted assets, § 217.10(b)(3). Arithmetic: 8% = 8 / 100 = 0.08. | Bare minimum; no buffer included. |
| Leverage ratio | 4% | § 217.10(a)(1)(iv) | Tier 1 capital divided by average total consolidated assets less deductions from tier 1 capital under § 217.22(a), (c) and (d), § 217.10(b)(4). Arithmetic: 4% = 4 / 100 = 0.04. | Separate from the risk-based ratios; not additive. |
| Supplementary leverage ratio, only for advanced approaches or Category III Board-regulated institutions | 3% | § 217.10(a)(1)(v) | Tier 1 capital divided by total leverage exposure, § 217.10(c)(1). Arithmetic: 3% = 3 / 100 = 0.03. | Additional institution-specific minimum; not a buffer and not applicable to all Board-regulated institutions. |

Provision text reproduced on the cited page

```text
§ 217.10 Minimum capital requirements.
(a) Minimum capital requirements.
(1) A Board-regulated institution must maintain the following minimum capital ratios:
(i) A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent.
(ii) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent.
(iii) A total capital ratio of 8 percent.
(iv) A leverage ratio of 4 percent.
(v) For advanced approaches Board-regulated institutions or, for Category III Board-regulated institutions, a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent.
```

Meaning of before buffers or add-ons

The table above reports only the § 217.10(a)(1) minima. It excludes any capital conservation buffer, stress capital buffer, countercyclical capital buffer, GSIB surcharge, or other buffer or add-on that would be layered on top of these floors elsewhere in Part 217. An institution subject to such an add-on must satisfy the minimum plus the applicable buffer or add-on; the amounts in this answer are the floors before that layering.

Institution-specific notes

1. Advanced approaches: after completing the parallel run process and receiving Board notification under § 217.121(d), an advanced approaches Board-regulated institution calculates its CET1, Tier 1 and Total capital ratios as the lower of the standardized calculation and the advanced approaches calculation under § 217.10(d)(1) through (3). The minimum percentage thresholds remain 4.5%, 6% and 8%.

2. Category III or advanced approaches: the supplementary leverage ratio minimum is 3% under § 217.10(a)(1)(v). The general leverage ratio minimum remains 4% under § 217.10(a)(1)(iv).

3. Qualifying community banking organization: under § 217.10(a)(2), a qualifying community banking organization subject to the community bank leverage ratio framework is considered to have met the minimum capital requirements in § 217.10(a). The CBLR framework has its own ratio, which is not reproduced on the cited page and is therefore not quantified here.

4. Historical transition: the 2014 phase-in values of 4.0% CET1 and 5.5% Tier 1 that appear in the transition provisions are historical and are not the current § 217.10(a)(1) minimums. They are not used in this answer.

Verification

All fetched copies of the cited text agree on the operative values: 4.5%, 6%, 8%, 4%, and the 3% supplementary leverage ratio for advanced approaches or Category III institutions. The hierarchy is internally consistent: 4.5% CET1 is below 6% Tier 1, which is below 8% Total capital. The leverage ratio and supplementary leverage ratio are separate, non-additive requirements. No currency conversion or rounding is involved because the figures are stated regulatory percentages.

Assumptions and limitations

This draft assumes the cited eCFR page is the operative text as of 2026-11-23 and that no later amendment changes § 217.10(a)(1). It assumes the institution is a Board-regulated institution that has not elected the community bank leverage ratio framework; if it has, § 217.10(a)(2) and the CBLR framework must be reviewed separately. This is a draft for review by a qualified finance, accounting or legal professional and is not regulatory, legal, tax or investment advice.

   following working day."

question: Y144
answer:
DRAFT FOR REVIEW BY A QUALIFIED TAX PROFESSIONAL — NOT TAX, LEGAL OR INVESTMENT ADVICE.

PERIOD: tax year 2025 (returns filed in 2026). CURRENCY: USD. BASIS: US federal individual income tax, statutory basis IRC section 1411, as described in IRS Publication 550 (2025). SOURCE EDITION: Publication 550 (2025), Investment Income and Expenses, 'For use in preparing 2025 Returns' — listed as current on https://www.irs.gov/publications and read at https://www.irs.gov/publications/p550 (HTML) and https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p550.pdf (PDF), fetched 2026-11-23.

=====================================================================
1. ANSWER
=====================================================================
1.1 RATE — 3.8% (decimal 0.038).
    Equivalent expressions: 0.038 = 3.8% = $38 of tax per $1,000 of base (0.038 x 1,000 = 38.00).

1.2 AMOUNT TO WHICH THE RATE IS APPLIED (the base) — the LESSER of two candidate amounts:
      (a) net investment income; or
      (b) the amount by which modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) exceeds the threshold amount for the filer's filing status.
    If (b) is zero or negative, the base is zero and no NIIT is due.

    Base = MIN( NII , MAX(0, MAGI - T) )
      where NII = net investment income (section 1411 definition)
            MAGI = modified adjusted gross income
            T = threshold amount by filing status (table 2.2 below)
      NIIT = 0.038 x Base

1.3 The rate is therefore NOT applied to all net investment income in every case. It is applied to the full net investment income only where MAGI exceeds the threshold by at least the amount of net investment income; otherwise the base is the (smaller) MAGI excess.

=====================================================================
2. SOURCE TEXT (both figures come from this single passage)
=====================================================================
2.1 Quoted verbatim from Pub. 550 (2025), General Information, item 'Net investment income tax (NIIT).':

    'The NIIT is a 3.8% tax on the lesser of your net investment income or the amount of your modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) that is over a threshold amount based on your filing status.'

    The HTML page (irs.gov/publications/p550) and the PDF (irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p550.pdf) render this paragraph word-for-word identically; the PDF text reads 'The NIIT is a 3.8% tax on the lesser of your net investment income or the amount of your modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) that is over a threshold amount based on your filing status.' No discrepancy between renderings.

2.2 Threshold table, as printed immediately after that paragraph in Pub. 550 (2025):

    Filing Status                                        Threshold Amount (USD)
    Married Filing Jointly or Qualifying Surviving Spouse      250,000
    Married Filing Separately                                  125,000
    Single or Head of Household                                200,000

2.3 Pub. 550 directs the reader onward for detail: 'See Code section 1411, Form 8960 and the Instructions for Form 8960 for more information.' That cross-reference is part of the sourced answer; the computation detail (what is included in net investment income, how MAGI is adjusted) is not set out in the quoted passage and must be taken from Form 8960 and its instructions.

=====================================================================
3. ARITHMETIC OF THE BASE — CANDIDATE AMOUNTS AND THE LESSER-OF SELECTION
=====================================================================
Step 1  Compute NII (candidate a). Source of components: section 1411 / Form 8960 — outside the Pub. 550 passage.
Step 2  Compute MAGI. Source: section 1411 / Form 8960 — outside the Pub. 550 passage.
Step 3  Look up T from table 2.2 by filing status.
Step 4  MAGI excess (candidate b) = MAGI - T. If the result is negative, use 0 (the tax cannot be applied to a negative amount; Pub. 550's phrase is 'the amount ... that is over a threshold', which is nil when MAGI is at or below the threshold).
Step 5  Base = the smaller of Step 1 and Step 4.
Step 6  NIIT = 0.038 x Base.

Control check applied to every illustration below: 0 <= NIIT <= 0.038 x NII and 0 <= NIIT <= 0.038 x MAGI excess. Any figure breaching either bound signals an error in the lesser-of selection.

=====================================================================
4. WORKED ILLUSTRATIONS (hypothetical figures, USD, tax year 2025)
=====================================================================
These are arithmetic demonstrations only; they are not a computation for any actual taxpayer.

4.1 Single filer; NII 60,000.00; MAGI 230,000.00
    T (Single) = 200,000.00                       [table 2.2]
    Candidate (a) NII                =  60,000.00
    Candidate (b) MAGI - T = 230,000.00 - 200,000.00 = 30,000.00
    Base = MIN(60,000.00, 30,000.00) =  30,000.00
    NIIT = 0.038 x 30,000.00         =   1,140.00
    Checks: 1,140.00 <= 0.038 x 60,000.00 = 2,280.00  OK
            1,140.00 <= 0.038 x 30,000.00 = 1,140.00  OK (binding constraint is (b))

4.2 Married filing jointly; NII 40,000.00; MAGI 600,000.00
    T (MFJ) = 250,000.00                          [table 2.2]
    Candidate (a) NII                =  40,000.00
    Candidate (b) MAGI - T = 600,000.00 - 250,000.00 = 350,000.00
    Base = MIN(40,000.00, 350,000.00) =  40,000.00
    NIIT = 0.038 x 40,000.00         =   1,520.00
    Checks: 1,520.00 <= 0.038 x 40,000.00 = 1,520.00  OK (binding constraint is (a))
            1,520.00 <= 0.038 x 350,000.00 = 13,300.00 OK
    Point: here the rate applies to ALL of NII — the common case, but only because (b) exceeds (a).

4.3 Married filing jointly; NII 90,000.00; MAGI 240,000.00
    T (MFJ) = 250,000.00                          [table 2.2]
    Candidate (b) MAGI - T = 240,000.00 - 250,000.00 = (10,000.00) -> floored at 0.00
    Base = MIN(90,000.00, 0.00) = 0.00
    NIIT = 0.038 x 0.00 = 0.00
    Point: MAGI below the threshold means no NIIT regardless of the size of NII.

4.4 Married filing separately; NII 10,000.00; MAGI 140,000.00
    T (MFS) = 125,000.00                          [table 2.2]
    Candidate (a) NII                =  10,000.00
    Candidate (b) MAGI - T = 140,000.00 - 125,000.00 = 15,000.00
    Base = MIN(10,000.00, 15,000.00) =  10,000.00
    NIIT = 0.038 x 10,000.00         =     380.00
    Checks: 380.00 <= 0.038 x 10,000.00 = 380.00 OK; 380.00 <= 0.038 x 15,000.00 = 570.00 OK

4.5 Summary tie-out table (all figures USD, tax year 2025)
    Case | Status | NII        | MAGI        | T        | (b)=MAGI-T | Base       | NIIT
    4.1  | Single |  60,000.00 |  230,000.00 | 200,000  |  30,000.00 |  30,000.00 | 1,140.00
    4.2  | MFJ    |  40,000.00 |  600,000.00 | 250,000  | 350,000.00 |  40,000.00 | 1,520.00
    4.3  | MFJ    |  90,000.00 |  240,000.00 | 250,000  |       0.00 |       0.00 |     0.00
    4.4  | MFS    |  10,000.00 |  140,000.00 | 125,000  |  15,000.00 |  10,000.00 |   380.00
    Total NIIT across the four illustrative cases = 1,140.00 + 1,520.00 + 0.00 + 380.00 = 3,040.00. Each line ties to its own Base x 0.038; the total ties to the sum of the four bases (30,000 + 40,000 + 0 + 10,000 = 80,000) x 0.038 = 3,040.00. OK.

=====================================================================
5. DISAMBIGUATION — 'NET INVESTMENT INCOME' HAS TWO MEANINGS IN PUB. 550
=====================================================================
5.1 NIIT base (section 1411). The quoted General Information paragraph, sourced to Code section 1411 and Form 8960. This is the meaning used in this answer.
5.2 Investment interest expense limitation (chapter 3 of Pub. 550). Pub. 550 states: 'Determine the amount of your net investment income by subtracting your investment expenses (other than interest expense) from your investment income' and 'Generally, your deduction for investment interest expense is limited to your net investment income.' This is a different measure used for the section 163(d) deduction limit and is NOT the NIIT base. A preparer must not substitute one for the other. Flagged because both appear in the same publication under the same label.

=====================================================================
6. SCOPE LIMITS AND ITEMS THE QUOTED PASSAGE DOES NOT RESOLVE
=====================================================================
Each item below is named as a limit, not answered with an unsourced figure.
6.1 Estates and trusts. Pub. 550's quoted table covers individual filing statuses only. Section 1411 applies a separate threshold to estates and trusts, set by reference to the top bracket under section 1(e). The 2025 dollar amount is NOT in the quoted passage and is not stated here; obtain it from the 2025 Instructions for Form 8960 or the applicable annual inflation Revenue Procedure before use.

MEMO — SOLVENCY CAPITAL REQUIREMENT CALIBRATION IN DIRECTIVE 2009/138/EC: STATED PROBABILITY, STATED HORIZON, AND EQUIVALENT RUIN FREQUENCY

Draft for review by a qualified finance/accounting or actuarial professional. Not legal, tax or investment advice. All figures below carry their source provision and their arithmetic.

=====================================================================
1. ANSWER IN BRIEF
=====================================================================

| Item | Answer | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Probability stated for the SCR | Confidence level of 99,5 % (Value-at-Risk) | STATED in the Directive | Art. 101(3), 2nd subparagraph |
| Implied probability of breaching the SCR / ruin per year | 0,5 % p.a. (= 100 % - 99,5 %) | DERIVED from the stated confidence level | Arithmetic on Art. 101(3) |
| Time horizon stated for the SCR | One-year period (existing business plus new business expected to be written over the following 12 months) | STATED in the Directive | Art. 101(3), 1st and 2nd subparagraphs |
| Equivalent ruin frequency | Once in 200 years — a mean return period of 200 years, i.e. a 1-in-200-year event | DERIVED: 1 / (1 - 0,995) = 1 / 0,005 = 200 | Arithmetic on Art. 101(3) |

Key caveat (read before relying on the last row): the Directive's own wording expresses the calibration as a Value-at-Risk at a 99,5 % confidence level over a one-year period. The Directive does not itself use a 'once in N years' formulation. The 1-in-200-years figure is the exact arithmetic equivalent of the Directive's stated confidence level and horizon, and is the formulation used in the Level 2 material and supervisory practice; it is presented here as a derived equivalence, not as a verbatim quotation from the Directive.

=====================================================================
2. SOURCE AND BASIS
=====================================================================

- Instrument: Directive 2009/138/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2009 on the taking-up and pursuit of the business of Insurance and Reinsurance (Solvency II) (recast), OJ L 335, 17.12.2009, p. 1-155; CELEX 32009L0138.
- Language version read: English.
- Text version relied on: 'Original (As adopted by EU)' — the version as it stood when first adopted, with no changes applied — as republished on legislation.gov.uk (eurdr/2009/138), plus the EUR-Lex CELEX landing pages for identification of the instrument.
- Provision in scope: Title I, Chapter VI (Rules relating to the valuation of assets and liabilities, technical provisions, own funds, Solvency Capital Requirement, Minimum Capital Requirement and investment rules), Section 4 (Solvency capital requirement), Subsection 1 (General provisions for the solvency capital requirement using the standard formula or an internal model), Article 101 (Calculation of the Solvency Capital Requirement), paragraph 3.
- Basis of the numbers: a regulatory calibration expressed as a probability (confidence level) over a defined period. No monetary amounts are involved; no currency applies. All percentages are as printed in the Directive, which uses a comma decimal separator ('99,5 %').

=====================================================================
3. THE OPERATIVE PROVISION — VERBATIM
=====================================================================

Article 101(3) of Directive 2009/138/EC (original, as adopted), verbatim:

  '3. The Solvency Capital Requirement shall be calibrated so as to ensure that all quantifiable risks to which an insurance or reinsurance undertaking is exposed are taken into account. It shall cover existing business, as well as the new business expected to be written over the following 12 months. With respect to existing business, it shall cover only unexpected losses.

  It shall correspond to the Value-at-Risk of the basic own funds of an insurance or reinsurance undertaking subject to a confidence level of 99,5 % over a one-year period.'

Context (Article 101(1) and (2), same source, verbatim):

  '1. The Solvency Capital Requirement shall be calculated in accordance with paragraphs 2 to 5.'

  '2. The Solvency Capital Requirement shall be calculated on the presumption that the undertaking will pursue its business as a going concern.'

Article 101(4) and (5) (verbatim, for completeness) list the risks to be covered — non-life, life and health underwriting risk, market risk, credit risk, operational risk — and require account to be taken of risk-mitigation techniques. Neither paragraph restates or alters the probability or the horizon; the calibration figure appears once, in Article 101(3).

=====================================================================
4. STATED FIGURES, WITH ARITHMETIC
=====================================================================

4.1 Probability (stated)
  Stated value: confidence level 99,5 % (Value-at-Risk of basic own funds).
  Source: Art. 101(3), 2nd subparagraph ('... subject to a confidence level of 99,5 % ...').
  Note on what this is a probability of: it is the confidence level of a Value-at-Risk on basic own funds, i.e. the SCR is set at the level of loss in basic own funds that is exceeded with 0,5 % probability over the horizon. It is not expressed in the Directive as a 'probability of ruin' or 'probability of default' as such; the 0,5 % tail probability is the equivalent reading.

4.2 Time horizon (stated)
  Stated value: one year.
  Source: Art. 101(3), 2nd subparagraph ('... over a one-year period').
  Corroborating horizon language in the same paragraph: the SCR 'shall cover existing business, as well as the new business expected to be written over the following 12 months' — i.e. a 12-month forward window, consistent with the one-year period.

4.3 Implied annual ruin probability (derived)
  Arithmetic: 100,0 % - 99,5 % = 0,5 % per annum.
  Basis: complement of the stated confidence level. This is an arithmetic identity, not an additional statement in the Directive.

4.4 Equivalent ruin frequency (derived)
  Arithmetic: 1 / 0,5 % = 1 / 0,005 = 200 years.
  Equivalently, as a frequency: 0,005 per annum = once in 200 years = a '1-in-200-year event'.
  Consistency check: 0,5 % x 200 = 100 % (the full probability mass is exhausted over 200 annual periods); 1 - 0,995 = 0,005 (the complement used is exactly the Directive's own figure).
  Interpretation: 200 years is the mean return period of the SCR-breach event under a stationary annual loss distribution — the mean of the geometric distribution with p = 0,005, which is 1/p = 200. It is not a claim that a breach will occur exactly every 200 years.

=====================================================================
5. WHAT THE DIRECTIVE DOES NOT SAY (PROVENANCE CAVEAT)
=====================================================================

- The Directive's original text does not contain the phrase 'once in 200 years', '1-in-200', '200-year event', or any other explicit return-period formulation. It states a 99,5 % confidence level over a one-year period and nothing more on calibration.
- The '1-in-200-years' formulation is the conventional regulatory and market gloss on that calibration and appears in Level 2/Level 3 material (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 and EIOPA guidance). Those texts were not retrieved and verified in this session; treat the attribution of the phrasing to those instruments as unverified background, flagged for the reviewer. The figure itself (200 years) does not depend on that attribution — it follows arithmetically from Article 101(3) alone.
- Recitals of the Directive were not retrieved and verified in this session. No reliance is placed on any recital; the operative calibration is in Article 101(3).
- Later amendments: the wording quoted above is from the as-adopted (original) version. Amendments made after adoption (e.g. by Omnibus II, Directive 2014/51/EU, and the Solvency II review amendments) were not checked here; the figure in Article 101(3) is the one the question asks about, and the reviewer should confirm whether any consolidated version in use in their jurisdiction renumbers or re-words it.
- The UK 'EU Exit' version of the same Article 101 shown on legislation.gov.uk carries the identical calibration wording (99,5 %, one-year period); it is noted only because that is the retrieval route for the original text, and no substantive difference was observed in the paragraphs quoted.

=====================================================================
6. POINTS FOR THE REVIEWING PROFESSIONAL
=====================================================================

1. Precision of language: the Directive calibrates the SCR as a Value-at-Risk on basic own funds at 99,5 % over one year. It does not define 'ruin' or 'insolvency probability'. If a document you are reviewing asserts that 'the Directive requires a 0,5 % probability of ruin', the accurate statement is that the Directive requires a 99,5 % one-year VaR, whose equivalent tail probability is 0,5 % per annum (a 1-in-200-year event).
2. Horizon: the one-year period is the risk horizon. It is distinct from the run-off / going-concern assumptions in Article 101(2) and from the 12-month new-business window in Article 101(3).
3. No currency: no monetary amount is set by the calibration provision; the SCR amount is undertaking-specific. Any figure in a downstream model that carries a currency must come from that model, not from Article 101.
4. Use of the 200-year figure: it is exact given the stated confidence level (1 / 0,005 = 200). Rounding to 'about 200 years' or 'a 1-in-200-year event' is acceptable; quoting any other return period (e.g. 100 or 250 years) would not agree with the Directive's stated 99,5 %.

=====================================================================
7. SOURCE-VERIFICATION LOG
=====================================================================

- https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eudr/2009/138/article/101/data.xht?view=snippet&wrap=true — verbatim Article 101(1)-(5) of Directive 2009/138/EC, including the '99,5 %' / 'one-year period' sentence; fetched 2026-11-23T12:04:50Z, sha256 ce93646eb35f.
- https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eudr/2009/138/article/101 — same Article; page identifies the version as 'Original (As adopted by EU)'; fetched 2026-11-23T12:04:04Z, sha256 01828fe1d6cb.
- https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/en/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32009L0138 and https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32009L0138 — EUR-Lex records for the instrument (identification of Directive 2009/138/EC, CELEX 32009L0138); listed as sources but the calibration sentence was read from the legislation.gov.uk as-adopted text above.
- Not retrieved/verified in this session: the recitals of Directive 2009/138/EC; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35; EIOPA guidance; any consolidated version incorporating post-2009 amendments.

=====================================================================
8. ONE-LINE ANSWER
=====================================================================

Article 101(3) of Directive 2009/138/EC (original text, as adopted) sets the SCR as the Value-at-Risk of basic own funds at a confidence level of 99,5 % over a one-year period; the equivalent ruin frequency is 1 / (1 - 0,995) = 1 / 0,005 = 200 years, i.e. a 1-in-200-year event (0,5 % per annum).

====================================================================
1. SCOPE, PERIOD, CURRENCY, BASIS
====================================================================
Entity type: FDIC-supervised institution (12 CFR Part 329 applies).
As-of date / period: the institution's 'calculation date' as that term is used in 329.21; no specific calendar date was supplied, so no dated period is asserted. Every figure below is "as of the calculation date."
Currency: US dollars (USD). All amounts in millions of USD unless stated.

Basis of the output figures: the regulatory liquid asset amounts defined in 329.21(b)(2) and 329.21(b)(3) — i.e., a fixed percentage of fair value — NOT fair value itself, and NOT the cap-constrained HQLA amount of 329.21(a).
Constraint applied (ask 1): other caps and adjustments are IGNORED. Specifically excluded: the level 2 cap excess amount (329.21(d), the 0.6667 x level 1 factor), the level 2B cap excess amount (329.21(e), the 0.1765 x (level 1 + level 2A) factor), the unadjusted and adjusted excess HQLA amounts (329.21(c), (g)), the adjusted liquid asset amounts arising from unwinding transactions maturing within 30 calendar days (329.21(f)), and the Regulation D reserve balance requirement deduction (329.21(b)(1), which applies to level 1 only).
Status: draft prepared for review by a qualified finance/accounting professional. Not regulatory, tax or investment advice.

====================================================================
2. OPERATIVE REGULATORY TEXT (SOURCE OF THE PERCENTAGES)
====================================================================
Source: 12 CFR 329.21(b), as reproduced on the cited page — eCFR, 12 CFR Part 329, section 329.21 (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-III/subchapter-B/part-329/section-329.21, fetched 2026-11-23T12:08:43Z, sha256 ca896132ac72). 329.21(b)(2): "Level 2A liquid asset amount. The level 2A liquid asset amount equals 85 percent of the fair value of all level 2A liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA."

329.21(b)(3): "Level 2B liquid asset amount. The level 2B liquid asset amount equals 50 percent of the fair value of all level 2B liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA."

Implied haircuts: level 2A 15% (100% - 85%); level 2B 50% (100% - 50%). Only these two percentages enter the requested figures.

====================================================================
3. INPUTS (EACH LABELLED AS GIVEN OR ASSUMED)
====================================================================
I-1  Fair value of eligible level 2A liquid assets ............ $80,000,000   [GIVEN in request]
I-2  Fair value of eligible level 2B liquid assets ............ $30,000,000   [GIVEN in request]
I-3  Level 2A percentage per 329.21(b)(2) ..................... 85% = 0.85   [SOURCE: quoted text, section 2]
I-4  Level 2B percentage per 329.21(b)(3) ..................... 50% = 0.50   [SOURCE: quoted text, section 2]
A-1  [ASSUMPTION] The stated amounts are fair value on the regulatory basis used in 329.21 (i.e., no further valuation adjustment is required before applying the percentages). If a reviewer determines otherwise, the percentages apply to the corrected fair value, not to these inputs.
A-2  [ASSUMPTION] All stated assets are eligible HQLA as of the calculation date (given in the request), so 329.22 operational and generally-applicable criteria are satisfied and no exclusion is made.
A-3  [ASSUMPTION] No level 1 liquid assets are in scope of this calculation (none were provided); the level 1 liquid asset amount is therefore not computed and is not needed because the caps that would use it are excluded per ask 1.
A-4  [ASSUMPTION] No assets are held in a foreign jurisdiction requiring the currency/jurisdiction conditions in 329.20(b)(2)(ii) or 329.20(b)(3)(2)(ii) to be tested; classification as level 2A/level 2B is taken as given.

====================================================================
4. CALCULATION — LEVEL 2A LIQUID ASSET AMOUNT
====================================================================
Formula (329.21(b)(2)): Level 2A liquid asset amount = 0.85 x fair value of eligible level 2A liquid assets
Arithmetic: 0.85 x $80,000,000 = $68,000,000
  80,000,000 x 0.85 = 80,000,000 x (0.80 + 0.05) = 64,000,000 + 4,000,000 = 68,000,000
Haircut retained against the institution: $80,000,000 - $68,000,000 = $12,000,000 (15%).
RESULT: Level 2A liquid asset amount = $68,000,000.

====================================================================
5. CALCULATION — LEVEL 2B LIQUID ASSET AMOUNT
====================================================================
Formula (329.21(b)(3)): Level 2B liquid asset amount = 0.50 x fair value of eligible level 2B liquid assets
Arithmetic: 0.50 x $30,000,000 = $15,000,000
  30,000,000 x 0.50 = 15,000,000
Haircut retained against the institution: $30,000,000 - $15,000,000 = $15,000,000 (50%).
RESULT: Level 2B liquid asset amount = $15,000,000.

====================================================================
6. CALCULATION — SUM (ASK 3)
====================================================================
Level 2A liquid asset amount ........ $68,000,000
Level 2B liquid asset amount ........ $15,000,000
Sum (level 2A + level 2B) ........... $83,000,000
Check: 68,000,000 + 15,000,000 = 83,000,000. In millions: 68 + 15 = 83.
RESULT: Sum = $83,000,000.

====================================================================
7. SUMMARY TABLE (USD, AS OF THE CALCULATION DATE)
====================================================================
Line | Item                                   | Fair value   | Percentage (source)      | Liquid asset amount | Arithmetic
-----+----------------------------------------+--------------+--------------------------+---------------------+----------------------------
  1  | Level 2A liquid assets (eligible HQLA) | 80,000,000   | 85% — 329.21(b)(2)       | 68,000,000          | 0.85 x 80,000,000
  2  | Level 2B liquid assets (eligible HQLA) | 30,000,000   | 50% — 329.21(b)(3)       | 15,000,000          | 0.50 x 30,000,000
  3  | Sum of lines 1 + 2                     | 110,000,000  | n/a (not a haircut line) | 83,000,000          | 68,000,000 + 15,000,000

Total fair value of the in-scope level 2 assets is $110,000,000; total haircut retained is $27,000,000 (12,000,000 + 15,000,000), which equals 110,000,000 - 83,000,000 — consistent.

====================================================================
8. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED (ASK 1 CONSTRAINT)
====================================================================
The following provisions of the cited page are reproduced in the source but are switched OFF for this calculation, exactly as instructed. They are listed so a reviewer can see they were considered and excluded, not overlooked:
(a) 329.21(a)(4) / 329.21(c)-(e) — unadjusted excess HQLA amount, comprising the level 2 cap excess amount (greater of [level 2A + level 2B - 0.6667 x level 1] and 0) and the level 2B cap excess amount (greater of [level 2B - level 2 cap excess - 0.1765 x (level 1 + level 2A)] and 0). The 0.6667 factor is the 40%-of-level-1 level 2 cap; the 0.1765 factor is the 15%-of-level-1 level 2B cap.
(b) 329.21(f)-(i) — adjusted liquid asset amounts and the adjusted excess HQLA amount arising from unwinding secured funding/lending, asset exchanges and collateralized derivatives transactions maturing within 30 calendar days.

1. **§ 252.72(a) — general limit.** 'No covered company may have an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital of the covered company.' (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/section-252.72, fetched 2026-11-23T12:13:56Z, sha256 cfa98394af04.)

Subpart Q source note reads '83 FR 38501, Aug. 6, 2018, as amended at 84 FR 59121, Nov. 1, 2019'. (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-II/subchapter-A/part-252/subpart-Q, fetched 2026-11-23T12:13:57Z, sha256 309a7a71aaca; .../subpart-H/section-252.176, sha256 7ba9a4280dbc.)

---

## 5. Ask 3 — dollar amount by which the exposure exceeds the cap

Excess = B - Cap = 11,000,000,000 - 10,000,000,000 = **1,000,000,000 USD**

Supporting ratios (all on the same basis and date):

| Measure | Arithmetic | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Exposure as % of tier 1 capital | 11,000,000,000 / 40,000,000,000 | 27.5% |
| Cap as % of tier 1 capital | 10,000,000,000 / 40,000,000,000 | 25.0% |
| Excess as % of tier 1 capital | 1,000,000,000 / 40,000,000,000 | 2.5% |
| Ratio check | 27.5% - 25.0% | 2.5% (agrees) |

**Answer to ask 3: $1,000,000,000 (one billion dollars) over the cap — a breach of § 252.72(a), which prohibits exposure 'that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital'. The position is not compliant; the exposure must be reduced, capital increased, or both (see §9).**

---

## 6. Ask 4 — is the 5% economic-interdependence / control-relationship assessment triggered?

Threshold = D x A = 0.05 x 40,000,000,000 = 2,000,000,000 USD

Test: is B > threshold? 11,000,000,000 > 2,000,000,000 → **YES, triggered.**

| Measure | Arithmetic | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 5% threshold in dollars | 0.05 x 40,000,000,000 | 2,000,000,000 |
| Exposure over the threshold | 11,000,000,000 - 2,000,000,000 | 9,000,000,000 |
| Exposure as a multiple of the threshold | 11,000,000,000 / 2,000,000,000 | 5.5x |
| Exposure as % of tier 1 capital (same figure as §5) | 11,000,000,000 / 40,000,000,000 | 27.5% (> 5%) |

**Answer to ask 4: Yes — the § 252.76(a)(1) assessment obligation is triggered.**

What 'triggered' does and does not mean:

- It is an **obligation to perform and document an assessment**, not a 5% exposure cap. Nothing in § 252.76 prohibits an exposure above 5% of tier 1 capital; the 5% figure is a threshold that switches on the analysis. (See §7(a).)
- The obligation is triggered by the size of the exposure alone. It is independent of the 25% breach in §5, and it is met here with 9,000,000,000 of headroom to spare.
- The **consequence is conditional**. Only if a factor in § 252.76(b)(2) (economic interdependence) or § 252.76(c)(1) (control relationship) is met — or the Board determines aggregation under § 252.76(d) — must the covered company aggregate its net credit exposure to the related counterparties 'for all purposes under this subpart, including … § 252.72'. Aggregation would raise the numerator and enlarge the breach quantified in §5; it cannot reduce it.
- The covered company may seek a written Board determination under § 252.76(b)(3) that identified counterparties are not economically interdependent.
- Because the 25% cap is already breached, the assessment cannot prudently be deferred: any aggregation finding increases an existing excess.

---

## 7. Framing points a reviewer should carry forward

**(a) The 5% figure is a trigger, not a limit.** The request describes a 'separate 5% … limit'. On the fetched text there is no 5% hard cap in Subpart H or Subpart Q. § 252.76(a)(1) / § 252.176(a)(2)(i) impose an assessment duty at 5% of tier 1 capital; the hard caps are 25% (§ 252.72(a) / § 252.172(b)) and, for major covered companies versus major counterparties, 15% (§ 252.72(b) / § 252.172(c)(2)). Any internal policy that treats 5% as a hard limit is an institution-specific appetite statement, not the rule.

**(b) Counterparty parent/affiliate status does not change the answer on the fetched text.** The fetched rule text contains no separate 5% (or other) cap keyed to whether the counterparty is the covered company's parent or a U.S. or non-U.S. affiliate. § 252.72 contains only (a) 25% and (b) 15%. If the reviewer's version of Part 252 (or an institution-specific interpretation) contains such a provision, re-run at that ratio; asks 2 and 3 are otherwise unaffected by counterparty status unless the 15% limb in (c) below applies.

**(c) The 15% limb is assumed inapplicable.** If the covered company were a 'major covered company' and the counterparty a 'major counterparty' (§ 252.71), the binding limit would be 0.15 x 40,000,000,000 = 6,000,000,000 and the excess 11,000,000,000 - 6,000,000,000 = 5,000,000,000. The request asks for the 25% cap, and the company is assumed not to be a major covered company facing a major counterparty. Confirm this before relying on the $10,000,000,000 figure as the binding constraint.

**(d) Subpart Q gives the same numbers.** For a U.S. intermediate holding company that is a covered foreign entity, § 252.172(b)(1) is also 25% of tier 1 capital → cap 10,000,000,000, excess 1,000,000,000; and § 252.176(a)(2)(i) is also a 5% assessment trigger → threshold 2,000,000,000, triggered. Note the different capital base: for a foreign banking organization under § 252.172(b)(2), the 25% is measured against the tier 1 capital of the foreign banking organization, not the combined U.S. operations.

---

## 8. Scenario table (so the reviewer can see what moves the answer)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Base case — covered company, ordinary counterparty (§ 252.72(a)) | 25% | 10,000,000,000 | 1,000,000,000 | 2,000,000,000 | Yes |

| Tier 1 capital revised down to $35,000,000,000 (illustrative) | 25% | 8,750,000,000 | 2,250,000,000 | 1,750,000,000 | Yes |
| Aggregation under § 252.76(a)(2) adds $2,000,000,000 of exposure (illustrative) | 25% | 10,000,000,000 | 3,000,000,000 | 2,000,000,000 | Yes |

(Illustrative rows use the same 25%/5% ratios and are shown only to demonstrate sensitivity: cap = 0.25 x capital; excess = 11,000,000,000 - cap, except the aggregation row where exposure = 13,000,000,000; threshold = 0.05 x capital. The aggregation row: 0.25 x 35,000,000,000 is not used; 13,000,000,000 - 10,000,000,000 = 3,000,000,000. The $35,000,000,000 row: 0.25 x 35,000,000,000 = 8,750,000,000; 11,000,000,000 - 8,750,000,000 = 2,250,000,000; 0.05 x 35,000,000,000 = 1,750,000,000.)

---

## 9. Remediation arithmetic (illustrative, for the reviewer's sizing only)

The rule itself does not prescribe a cure period; the appropriate remediation, notification and disclosure response is a governance and supervisory question for the reviewer, not a computation.

1. **Two-day snapshot gap.** The 'as in force on 2026-11-21' text was read from eCFR 'current' pages fetched 2026-11-23. Confirm no amendment took effect on 2026-11-22 or 2026-11-23. # Draft — Item 402(c) Perquisite Disclosure Analysis

Prepared for review by a qualified finance or legal professional. This is a draft, not legal, tax or compliance advice.

## 1. Scope, period, currency and basis

- Registrant: [registrant]
- Executive: [named executive officer]
- Period: one covered fiscal year, [FY____] — assumed because the request does not state the fiscal year.
- Currency: US dollars (USD).
- Basis: aggregate incremental cost to the registrant, as required for perquisites and personal benefits under Item 402(c)(2)(ix) and its instructions. This basis is assumed for both items.
- Facts assumed: the $24,000 and $26,000 amounts are each a separate perquisite or personal benefit; neither falls within a categorical exclusion; the registrant is not relying on scaled Item 402(n) disclosure. If either amount is an aggregate of multiple perquisites, the conclusion may change and each underlying perquisite must be tested separately unless aggregation by type is permitted.

## 2. Rule text applied

17 CFR 229.402(c)(2)(ix), Instructions to Item 402(c)(2)(ix), Instruction 4 provides:

Perquisites and personal benefits may be excluded as long as the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits for a named executive officer is less than $10,000. If the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits is $10,000 or more for any named executive officer, then each perquisite or personal benefit, regardless of its amount, must be identified by type. If perquisites and personal benefits are required to be reported for a named executive officer pursuant to this rule, then each perquisite or personal benefit that exceeds the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the total amount of perquisites and personal benefits for that officer must be quantified and disclosed in a footnote.

Source: eCFR 17 CFR 229.402, Instructions to Item 402(c)(2)(ix), Instruction 4; also CFR-2025 title 17, volume 3, section 229.402. The eCFR current text fetched 2026-11-23 contains this instruction, and I identified no amendment affecting it. Note: the project-context phrase referring to the greater of $10,000 and 25% is not the rule text; the operative footnote-quantification text is the greater of $25,000 or 10%.

## 3. Test 1 — May the registrant exclude perquisites altogether?

- Total perquisites and personal benefits: $120,000 (source: request facts).
- Exclusion threshold: total must be less than $10,000.
- Comparison: $120,000 is greater than or equal to $10,000.
- Conclusion: No. The registrant may not exclude the perquisites altogether. Because the total is $10,000 or more, each perquisite or personal benefit, regardless of its amount, must be identified by type and included in All Other Compensation in column (i).

The $10,000 rule is an exclusion and identification threshold. It is not the footnote-quantification threshold.

## 4. Test 2 — Footnote quantification threshold

- 10% of total perquisites and personal benefits: $120,000 × 10% = $12,000.
- Statutory floor: $25,000.
- Footnote quantification threshold: greater of $25,000 or $12,000 = $25,000.

Therefore, an individual perquisite or personal benefit must be quantified in a footnote only if its value exceeds $25,000.

## 5. Item-by-item application

| Item | Amount | Test: amount greater than $25,000? | Result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Item A | $24,000 | $24,000 > $25,000? No | Include and identify by type; no footnote quantification required under the perquisite rule. |
| Item B | $26,000 | $26,000 > $25,000? Yes | Must be quantified and disclosed in a footnote. |

Arithmetic checks: $24,000 < $25,000; $26,000 > $25,000; $12,000 < $25,000; $120,000 ≥ $10,000. No stated figure violates a threshold set in this memo.

## 6. Conclusion

- Ask 2: No. The registrant may not exclude perquisites altogether. Total perquisites and personal benefits of $120,000 are not less than $10,000.
- Ask 3: The footnote quantification threshold is the greater of $25,000 or 10% of total perquisites and personal benefits. Here, 10% × $120,000 = $12,000, so the operative threshold is $25,000.
- Ask 4: The $26,000 item must be quantified. The $24,000 item must be identified by type but is not quantified in a footnote under the perquisite rule because it does not exceed $25,000.

## 7. Illustrative footnote language

All Other Compensation includes perquisites and personal benefits with an aggregate incremental cost of $120,000. Each perquisite is identified by type. The [describe the $26,000 item] had an aggregate incremental cost of $26,000, which exceeded the greater of $25,000 and 10% of total perquisites and personal benefits ($12,000), and is quantified here.

## 8. Caveats

- If the $24,000 or $26,000 amount is not a perquisite or personal benefit but is other compensation reported under Item 402(c)(2)(ix), Instruction 3 applies: any such item exceeding $10,000 must be identified and quantified in a footnote. Under that alternative, the $24,000 item would also require quantification.
- If either amount is an aggregate of multiple perquisites, test each underlying perquisite unless aggregation by type is permitted. The $26,000 conclusion assumes it is a single perquisite or personal benefit, or a properly aggregated type whose aggregate exceeds $25,000.
- The fiscal year and valuation date must be inserted. All figures are assumed to be USD and valued on the aggregate incremental cost basis.

MINIMUM CET1 AND TIER 1 RATIOS — ADVANCED APPROACHES NATIONAL BANK, CALENDAR YEAR 2014
Draft for review by a qualified finance/regulatory reporting professional. Not legal or regulatory advice.

=== 0. SCOPE, PERIOD, CURRENCY, BASIS ===
Entity: a national bank that is an advanced approaches institution and is not a savings and loan holding company (an SLHC is by definition a holding company, so a national bank cannot itself be an SLHC; the qualifier in the rule is descriptive and does not alter the result — see §6).
Regulator: OCC. Governing instrument: 12 CFR Part 3 (the OCC's 2013 capital rule, 78 FR 62018, Oct. 11, 2013, effective Jan. 1, 2014).
Period: January 1, 2014 through December 31, 2014 inclusive.
Currency: none stated. All figures are regulatory capital ratios — dimensionless percentages of risk-weighted assets. No USD amounts are computed here. RWA themselves are USD-denominated but are not quantified in this deliverable.
Basis: transitional (phase-in) minimum ratios under subpart G as implemented by 12 CFR 3.2(f), compared with the steady-state minimum ratios stated in 12 CFR 3.10(a). Buffers and all other add-ons excluded per the instruction (ask 3).

=== 1. ASK 1 — MINIMUM RATIOS THAT APPLIED 1 JAN 2014 – 31 DEC 2014 ===
Common equity tier 1 (CET1) minimum: 4.0 percent (= 0.0400)
Tier 1 capital minimum: 5.5 percent (= 0.0550)

Source (verbatim, 12 CFR 3.2(f)(1)(iii)(A)):
"Beginning on January 1, 2014, calculate and maintain minimum capital ratios in accordance with subparts A, B, and C of this part, provided, however, that such national bank or Federal savings association must: (A) From January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014, maintain a minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4 percent, a minimum tier 1 capital ratio of 5.5 percent, a minimum total capital ratio of 8 percent, and a minimum leverage ratio of 4 percent; and (B) From January 1, 2015 to December 31, 2017, an advanced approaches national bank or Federal savings association: ..."
Lead-in (12 CFR 3.2(f)(1)): "Subject to the transition provisions in subpart G of this part, an advanced approaches national bank or Federal savings association that is not a savings and loan holding company must: ..."
Pages on which this text was read: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-I/part-3 (sha256 9bf3368111e1) and https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2024-title12-vol1/xhtml/CFR-2024-title12-vol1-part3.html (sha256 f74bb08d7f12).
Arithmetic / conversion: 4 percent = 4/100 = 0.0400; 5.5 percent = 5.5/100 = 0.0550. Both figures are quoted directly from the rule; no computation is required to derive them. They are the operative regulatory minimums for the period, i.e. the numbers a 2014 legacy checklist should carry.
Out of scope but stated in the same sentence for completeness: total capital 8 percent; leverage ratio 4 percent (not requested).

=== 2. ASK 2 — CORRESPONDING MINIMUM RATIOS IN THE TEXT OF 12 CFR PART 3 ON THE CITED PAGE ===
Common equity tier 1 minimum in Part 3, § 3.10(a): 4.5 percent (= 0.0450)
Tier 1 capital minimum in Part 3, § 3.10(a): 6.0 percent (= 0.0600)

Source (verbatim, 12 CFR 3.10(a)(1), current eCFR):
"§ 3.10 Minimum capital requirements. (a) Minimum capital requirements. (1) A national bank or Federal savings association must maintain the following minimum capital ratios: (i) A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent. (ii) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent. (iii) A total capital ratio of 8 percent. (iv) A leverage ratio of 4 percent. (v) For advanced approaches national banks or Federal savings associations or, for Category III OCC-regulated institutions, a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent. (vi) For Federal savings associations, a tangible capital ratio of 1.5 percent."

Source (verbatim, 12 CFR 3.10(a), CFR-2014 title 12 volume 1 — the volume in force during 2014):
"§ 3.10 Minimum capital requirements. (a) Minimum capital requirements. A [BANK] must maintain the following minimum capital ratios: (1) A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent. (2) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent. (3) A total capital ratio of 8 percent. (4) A leverage ratio of 4 percent. (5) For advanced approaches [BANK]s, a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent."
Note: the CFR-2014 PDF renders the institution name as "[BANK]" — this is the OCC's model/placeholder formatting in the codified text, not a different rule. The substantive figures are identical across the 2014 codification and the current eCFR: 4.5 percent CET1 and 6 percent Tier 1.
Pages on which this text was read: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2014-title12-vol1/pdf/CFR-2014-title12-vol1-part3.pdf (sha256 42939370e38e) and https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-I/part-3 (sha256 9bf3368111e1).
Arithmetic / conversion: 4.5 percent = 4.5/100 = 0.0450; 6 percent = 6/100 = 0.0600. Quoted directly; no computation required.

=== 3. RECONCILIATION — WHY THE TWO SETS DIFFER (THIS IS THE MATERIAL FINDING) ===
| Ratio | Applied 1 Jan–31 Dec 2014 (transition, § 3.2(f)(1)(iii)(A)) | Stated in Part 3 § 3.10(a) (steady state) | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| CET1 | 4.0% (0.0400) | 4.5% (0.0450) | 0.5 pp (0.0050) |
| Tier 1 | 5.5% (0.0550) | 6.0% (0.0600) | 0.5 pp (0.0050) |
Arithmetic: 4.5 − 4.0 = 0.5 percentage points; 6.0 − 5.5 = 0.5 percentage points. As decimals: 0.0450 − 0.0400 = 0.0050; 0.0600 − 0.0550 = 0.0050. Check that both differences agree: they do (0.5 pp each).
Interpretation: § 3.10(a) states the fully effective minimums that a bank must meet once the phase-in completes. § 3.2(f)(1)(iii)(A) is the transitional override that sets a lower binding minimum for calendar 2014 only. A bank subject to the transition was required to meet the § 3.2(f) figure during 2014, not the § 3.10(a) figure. From January 1, 2015 the § 3.10(a) levels (4.5% / 6.0%) became the applicable minimums, i.e. the phase-in was a two-step schedule: 2014 = 4.0% / 5.5%; 2015 and after = 4.5% / 6.0%.
Practical consequence for the reviewer: a legacy checklist that carries 4.0% / 5.5% for CY2014 is CORRECT for the transitional minimum but is NOT the same number as the § 3.10(a) text on the cited page (4.5% / 6.0%). Conversely, a checklist that carries 4.5% / 6.0% for CY2014 is quoting the steady-state standard and overstates the binding 2014 minimum by 0.5 pp on each ratio. Both numbers are correct statements about different provisions; they must not be conflated. If the checklist is scored against actual 2014 compliance, the applicable thresholds are 4.0% and 5.5%.

=== 4. EFFECT OF ADVANCED APPROACHES STATUS DURING 2014 ===
Advanced approaches status did not change the minimum ratio percentages in 2014. It changed (a) the risk-weighted-asset denominator and (b) the timing of RWA methodology adoption:
- 12 CFR 3.2(f)(1)(i): from January 1, 2014 the bank calculates advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets under subpart E (and subpart F if applicable); calculation of standardized total risk-weighted assets under subpart D begins January 1, 2015.
- 12 CFR 3.10(c) (2014 text) / 3.10(d) (current text): once the bank has completed the parallel run and received OCC notification under § 3.121(d), each ratio is the LOWER of the standardized ratio and the advanced approaches ratio. That is a measurement rule, not a minimum-ratio rule — it can only reduce the measured ratio, never change the 4.0% / 5.5% thresholds.
- During calendar 2014, because standardized RWA calculation did not begin until January 1, 2015, the lower-of test was not yet operative for a bank on the advanced approaches timeline; the 2014 ratio denominator was advanced approaches RWA. (Reviewer to confirm against the bank's specific parallel-run status and any OCC notification date.)
Net: the answer to ask 1 is unchanged by advanced approaches status. The 4.0% / 5.5% thresholds apply to the advanced approaches bank exactly as quoted.

=== 5. BUFFERS AND OTHER ADD-ONS — EXCLUDED (ASK 3) ===
The following are excluded from every figure above and were not added to any stated minimum:
- Capital conservation buffer (12 CFR 3.11) — 0 percent for calendar 2014; the buffer phase-in begins in calendar 2016 (0.625% in 2016, 1.25% in 2017, 1.875% in 2018, 2.5% from 2019). Because it did not exist in 2014, excluding it is not merely an instruction — it matches the rule in force. (Phase-in percentages to be verified against § 3.11(a) by the reviewer; they are context only and enter no calculation above.)
- Countercyclical capital buffer (12 CFR 3.11(b)) — not activated; excluded.
- G-SIB surcharge and any institution-specific buffer — excluded.
- Supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent for advanced approaches banks (§ 3.10(a)(1)(v) current / § 3.10(a)(5) in the 2014 text) — excluded as an add-on. It is in any event a leverage measure, not a risk-based CET1 or Tier 1 minimum, and its compliance date for advanced approaches banks is January 1, 2018.
- Prompt corrective action thresholds (12 CFR 6 / the 78 FR 62018 passage quoting "less than 6.0 percent" tier 1, "less than 4.5 percent" CET1, "less than 4.0 percent" tier 1, etc.) — these are PCA classification triggers, a different construct from the minimum capital requirements, and are excluded.
- Total capital ratio (8 percent) and leverage ratio (4 percent) — out of scope; noted only because they appear in the same operative sentences.

=== 6. THE 'NOT A SAVINGS AND LOAN HOLDING COMPANY' QUALIFIER ===
Immaterial to the numeric answer. 12 CFR 3.2(f)(1) is addressed to "an advanced approaches national bank or Federal savings association that is not a savings and loan holding company." A national bank is a depository institution, not a holding company, so it can never be an SLHC; the qualifier routes a national bank into § 3.2(f)(1) rather than § 3.2(f)(2) and does not alter the 4.0% / 5.5% figures. No adjustment is required.

=== 7. IDENTIFICATION OF 'THE CITED PAGE' — RESIDUAL AMBIGUITY, NOT A BLOCK ===
The request does not name the page. Two candidate pages were retrieved and both reproduce 12 CFR Part 3 with the same § 3.10(a) figures (CET1 4.5%, Tier 1 6.0%):
(a) eCFR current, https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-I/part-3 (sha256 9bf3368111e1);
(b) CFR 2014 edition, title 12 vol. 1, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2014-title12-vol1/pdf/CFR-2014-title12-vol1-part3.pdf (sha256 42939370e38e).
The answer to ask 2 is therefore stable across both the 2014 codification and the current codification: 4.5 percent / 6.0 percent. Note for the reviewer: if the cited page instead reproduces 12 CFR 3.2(f) rather than § 3.10(a), the figures on that page would read 4 percent / 5.5 percent — i.e. the ask 2 answer would equal the ask 1 answer. The distinction between the two provisions is the only thing that can move ask 2, and it is a question of which section the page reproduces, not of which edition of the CFR it is.

=== 8. NOTES FOR THE REVIEWER ===
1. The two answers are deliberately different. Ask 1 = the binding 2014 transitional minimum (4.0% / 5.5%). Ask 2 = the steady-state minimum in the codified text (4.5% / 6.0%). Do not reconcile them to a single number; report both, labelled.
2. If the deliverable is a compliance test of 2014 actuals, compare to 4.0% / 5.5%. If it is a checklist that must match the face of § 3.10, expect 4.5% / 6.0% and annotate the transition.
3. Confirm the bank's parallel-run status and any § 3.121(d) OCC notification date — this affects the denominator (lower-of test) from 2015, not the 2014 thresholds.
4. Confirm no early-adoption or opt-out election altered the bank's transition schedule. The rule as quoted contains no such election for the minimum ratios.
5. All figures are direct quotations from the regulatory text; no estimation, interpolation or assumption enters any number stated above. The only judgment calls are (i) which provision answers ask 2 (§ 3.10(a), as reasoned in §7) and (ii) the § 3.11 buffer phase-in percentages cited as context in §5, which enter no calculation.
